contracts_used: Named in the targets only, all from brief H-7: SourceFullCorrect (ChainLiftStatement, RecordAuthLiftStatement, RecordLiftStatement), FrameReadBack and DecoderAgreement (OriginStatement), FrameReadBack (BindingStatement); CtxAuthLift, CtxPrivLift, CtxLift, HidingStatement, FreshGuessStatement and LorStatement name none. IND$, INT-CTXT, HMAC-PRF and Extract-on-uniform32 appear only as advantages of explicit reductions; the BLAKE2b ROM is the lazily sampled shared cache of the world. The 28 theorems use no contract. No assumption or contract is added.
deviations_from_plan: CtxPrivLiftStatement is stated for both observation modes against randomRecords (equal to idealRecords in mode P by idealRecords_P); since the fix pass its mode-O instance has no consumer and is kept because the per-key privacy hop is uniform in the mode.

OriginStatement and BindingStatement are one-world event bounds, HidingStatement an exact law equality with derived Boolean and event forms, FreshGuessStatement a one-world bound and LorStatement an exact one-half equality; none is a two-sided comparison of two worlds, which is not their natural form.

The targets take their reductions and bill functions as parameters; closed-form bills and the concrete simulator-built reductions are fixed by the delivering stages. A target with artificial reductions is satisfiable trivially and is not a deliverable (guide, design panel section 1).
The view adds the environment state and the handle-to-slot map to the CE-12 analysis projection (needed by R6 and the origin event); this strengthens the targets.
R6 forms are not part of S1 (stage S6).
The bills include the decision coin cost (BillInput.decision), since reductions run the decision.
BindingStatement takes its cross-handle term as an explicit parameter (intended bindingTerm, fixed by BindingTarget), like the D3 terms.

LorStatement puts TestsHidden inside both events instead of the review proposal's premise that eligibility imply a public TestHidden; this holds for every eligibility, implies the premise form, and needs no public recomputation function (admission depends only on the mode-P view, admittedTest_view).
guessTerm omits the review's S^2/2^512 term: commitments of distinct seals are independent, and without it the term is at most the S1 term for every budget (guessTerm_le).
not_proved: Every target: chain_lift, ctx_lift (both halves and their composition), the integrity record lift, record_lift, idealRecords_origin (OriginStatement, BindingStatement), idealRecords_hiding (HidingStatement, FreshGuessStatement, LorStatement).
The all-real source equality of ctxRun with idealChains and one seal per material label in ctxRun (stage S4).

CE-12 obligations listed in the guide: frame-level CE-OR and CE-UKS events through codec.frameRead, and C5 as a support invariant of the client program with env_g for every interpreter (idealAuth, idealRecords), plus the C5 maps for CE-APP and CE-LOR.
checks_not_run: No lake build, make verify, nix-collect-garbage, mutation testing, ProVerif or Rust run in S1, the fix pass or the nit fix; no production Rust or ProVerif change. Transcript fidelity and the integration into central run after the nit fix on the merged tip (nit_fix.integration_checks).

findings.title: Earlier prose claim still unsupported: the module docstring and the analysis say random mode is a proven endpoint of the existing CTX bounds
findings.response: Module docstring line 9 and the analysis sentence reworded: real and replay are exactly the endpoints of selected_integrity (keyImpl_modes), and random mode agrees with replay except on sealing (randomImpl_other). The docstring worlds paragraph, the guide worlds section and CtxPrivLiftStatement paragraph say the IND$ correspondence is not proved; the guide open points list the correspondence of randomImpl with the IND$ random experiment behind replay_random_advantage as an explicit S4 obligation; design panel row KeyMode and lens item S4 updated.

findings.title: CE-12 obligation (ii) states only the forward direction of C5, which the containments need alongside 'slot_g is held only by the designated handles'
findings.response: Extended in the guide consumer paragraph, the open points and design A1: C5 must also give that only the designated handles hold slot_g on the support of every interpreter, from per-role slot uniqueness via PqxdhRecordLiftProtocol.Unused/markUsed plus C5 for both designated handles, or from the converse of C5. The analysis sentence on the two remaining CE-12 steps says the same in plain English.
